chapters.title: Let's set up your first habit.
chapters.purpose: Turn one small action into a clear identity-based habit mission.

pages.title: Let's set up your first habit.
pages.body: A small, easy mission can lead to a powerful change.

pages.title: A strong habit needs three things.
pages.body: An action, a time and place, and most of all, an identity. You are not only building a habit. You are becoming the person you want to be.

pages.title: Make it easy enough to begin now.
pages.body: 1. Name the habit. 2. Make it specific. 3. Tie it to who you want to become.

pages.title: Use this simple promise.
pages.body: I will [habit], [time and place], so I can become [the kind of person I want to be]. Example: I will meditate for five minutes when I wake up so I can become a mindful person.

pages.question: What small habit will you do?
When and where will you do it?
pages.placeholder: When I wake up, beside my bed

pages.question: Who will this help you become?

pages.title: Your first habit is ready.
pages.body: I will {{habit-action}}, {{habit-time-place}}, so I can become {{habit-identity}}. Read it once. Does it feel exciting and easy to keep?

pages.title: Your habit today.
pages.body: I will {{habit-action}}, {{habit-time-place}}, so I can become {{habit-identity}}.

chapters.title: Psst... your day has a rhythm.
chapters.purpose: Learn when the person feels most natural and what changes their energy.

pages.body: Three small answers may show when life feels easiest.

Where is it easiest for you to focus?

pages.body: Go back if one answer needs changing. Continue when it feels right.

pages.placeholder: Describe the kind of person, not their name.

pages.question: When life feels hard, what kind of support actually helps?

pages.title: Your way of connecting is clearer.

pages.question: Where do you feel most settled?

pages.question: What in your space bothers you more than it should?
pages.placeholder: Noise, mess, people, light, or something else.

pages.question: Where do you feel more awake?

pages.title: Your surroundings matter.
pages.body: Go back if needed. Continue when this feels like your real life.

pages.title: Three answers saved.

pages.body: Three answers may show what makes a choice feel like yours.

pages.placeholder: Keep it as simple as you want.

pages.question: How do you know when a choice feels right?
pages.placeholder: What do you notice in yourself?

pages.title: Your way of choosing is clearer.
pages.body: Read the answers once. Continue when they feel honest.

pages.title: Three answers saved.
pages.body: Athena can now be more careful when asking about plans and freedom.

pages.title: What if rest is more than doing nothing?
pages.body: Three answers can show what actually brings you back.

pages.question: What leaves you feeling truly rested?
pages.placeholder: Think of what works, not what should work.

pages.question: What kind of fun do you miss?
How easy is it for you to rest without feeling guilty?

pages.title: Rest means something specific to you.
pages.body: Change an answer if needed. Continue when it feels true.

pages.title: Three answers saved.
pages.body: Athena can now tell the difference between empty time and real rest.

chapters.title: Psst... what makes a day worth it?

pages.title: Psst... what makes a day worth it?
pages.body: Three answers can show what matters beneath goals and plans.

pages.question: What small moment can make a whole day feel worthwhile?

What do you want to protect from getting crowded out?
pages.placeholder: A person, practice, feeling, or part of yourself.

pages.title: These answers point toward what matters.
pages.body: Go back if needed. Continue when they sound like you.

pages.title: Three answers saved.
pages.body: Athena has better evidence about what makes life feel worthwhile to you.

pages.placeholder: It does not need to be useful.

What small sign shows that change may have already started?

pages.title: Growth is easier to see now.
pages.body: Review the answers. Continue when they feel honest.

pages.title: Three answers saved.

pages.title: You noticed a little more.

pages.body: Go back if you want. Continue when this feels true.

pages.title: What stood out is saved.

chapters.title: Before the day moves on...
chapters.purpose: Help the person notice support, what their body needs, and one kind next step.

pages.title: Before the day moves on...
pages.body: Take one quiet minute to listen in.

pages.question: Did anyone make today a little better? How?
What is your body asking for right now?
pages.placeholder: Rest, food, movement, quiet, or something else.

pages.question: What small kindness could you give yourself tonight?

pages.title: You listened to yourself.
pages.body: Go back if you want. Continue when the answers feel right.

pages.title: One kind thought is saved.
pages.body: It does not have to become a rule.

chapters.title: What should tomorrow carry?
chapters.purpose: Help the person choose what to repeat, release, and quietly hope for tomorrow.

pages.title: What should tomorrow carry?
pages.body: Keep what helps. Leave what does not.

pages.question: What part of today would you gladly repeat?
What do you want to leave behind when today ends?
What is one quiet hope for tomorrow?

pages.title: Tomorrow has a little more room.
pages.body: Go back if you want. Continue when this feels honest.

pages.title: Your thought for tomorrow is saved.
pages.body: You do not need to solve the whole day now.
